transcript:
Header: 2027-04-28 10:00 AM PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jared (NexaHealth CTO), Priya (SRE), Liam (ML Eng)

Summary: quick check-in, env readiness, access, bench runs, and security docs.

00:00 Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got a short agenda right? 
00:07 Maya: yep, quick recap — onboarding status, network/access, bench runs, security artifacts, next steps, any blockers. 
00:15 Priya: we finished the basic signup and token exchange last week. we still haven't completed VPC peering — that's blocking the private inference tests. 
00:23 Carlos: ok, that's what we want to validate first; the plan is to run the 5k token clinical note pipeline inside your VPC so we can measure tail latency and throughput. we'll bring the same model variant we used in the hosted tests. note: sometimes the KV cache behaves differently in private setups, so we'll watch that. 
00:40 Liam: quick question — do you need us to open anything on our side besides the peering? ports, sgs? 
00:48 Carlos: primarily peering and a set of egress rules for the control plane to reach the instance, and the service account key. also if you're using strict egress we need to allow the peering endpoints we sent earlier. 
00:58 Priya: right, I have the CIDR, but I need the exact subnets. Maya, you sent a doc but the names were kinda cut off in the PDF, can you re-send? 
01:07 Maya: yeah i'll resend the VPC peering checklist and the step-by-step SSO/SAML guide. i'll include the Azure/AWS snippets. 
01:15 Jared: on security, procurement asked for SOC2 and details on KMS integration. what do you have? 
01:22 Maya: we've got SOC2 Type II report; i'll share a sanitized copy and a KMS integration doc that shows how keys are rotated and how we surface audit logs. we can also do an architecture diagram for the private deployment. 
01:33 Liam: curious on data retention — pilot logs should be kept only 30 days. can you configure that on the Red Wood side? 
01:40 Carlos: yep we can set retention on the logging endpoint, and for the pilot we can route logs into your SIEM. note: sometimes the product name gets transcribed as "Red Wood" in older docs, but that's the same Redwood Inference. 
01:52 Priya: good. for pilot perf we care about p95 and p99, not just avg. 
01:57 Carlos: absolutely — we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and a token-level cost breakdown. also want to try a quantized 4-bit model to see cost savings; there will be some quality delta. 
02:09 Jared: can you remind me of the quantization tradeoffs? 
02:12 Carlos: sure — 4-bit typically reduces memory and increases throughput; latency may improve but some subtle hallucination or reduced scoring on edge cases. we recommended running evals on your prompt set. we'll run a small eval harness as part of the bench. 
02:27 Lily: (inaudible)
02:30 Liam: sorry, just to check — for the POC, are we evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity or the hosted API? 
02:36 Maya: initial pilot will be in your VPC via Private deploy (control plane managed), but we can show Dedicated pricing if you want reserved throughput later. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and cost at scale; hosted is faster to stand up. 
02:49 Priya: procurement also asked about SLA numbers — do you have a standard? 
02:52 Maya: for Dedicated we provide SLA backed uptime and latency targets; for hosted we have standard terms. i'll pull the exact SLA sheet. 
02:59 Jared: ok. timeline wise — we want to complete bench runs and security review in two weeks, so we can decide on go/no-go with procurement. 
03:06 Maya: sounds reasonable. Carlos, do you have everything to run the bench once peering is up? 
03:10 Carlos: yes — i'll need the subscription IDs, the peering acceptance, and a service account with limited permissions. we'll schedule the run during low traffic; bench should take ~3 hours but we'll collect metrics for 24 hours to see variance. 
03:24 Priya: i'll try to get the CIDR and service account in by tomorrow EOD. 
03:29 Maya: perfect. i'll send the SOC2 + KMS doc tonight. also sending our recommended bench script and a link to the bench dashboard (shared drive link). 
03:38 Jared: any blockers from your side? 
03:40 Liam: one small note — our dataset contains PHI. we need confirmation that logs redact PII and that SSO enforces RBAC for the pilot. 
03:48 Maya: we support field-level redaction and can show the config. SSO with SAML + SCIM for groups is supported, and RBAC mapping is available. i'll include mapping examples. 
03:59 Carlos: quick aside — we might try two model variants in the bench: the 1) base open model quantized 4-bit and 2) higher-precision variant for comparison. that'll give you cost vs quality numbers. 
04:12 Jared: great. can you also include a rough cost estimate for 100k tokens/day on both variants so procurement can see ballpark numbers? 
04:20 Maya: yes i'll add a ballpark cost spreadsheet. 
04:24 Priya: timeline notes: I'll try to have peering request in by tomorrow and confirm service account. procurement may be slower but we'll push. 
04:31 Maya: recap: Carlos runs bench when peering is accepted; Maya to send security artifacts and bench script tonight; Jared to confirm retention & PII fields; Priya to send subscription/CIDR. next sync same time next week unless we need an earlier dedicated pricing call. 
04:44 Jared: sounds good, thanks everyone. 
04:47 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links. bye.

Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (Red Wood vs Redwood, K-V cache as K-V cash), natural speech filler, slight crosstalk. References shared: [SOC2 doc link], [VPC peering checklist], [bench script & dashboard link], [pricing spreadsheet].

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items.

End of transcript.
